about: Data of Learn lesson A8, How long should storage last? The Plains Grid and its fleet are fictional and illustrative; demand, wind and solar follow the real hourly shapes of the Southwest Power Pool grid in 2025 (town_year.json, EIA-930), scaled as stated below. Storage parameters and costs come from the primary sources listed with each item. The reference block holds the week's results for each store, solved with HiGHS 1.15.1.

plains.name: Plains Grid
plains.note: Illustrative: a future Plains Grid with much wind and little firm power, so that a calm week leaves a gap. Not a forecast of any real grid.

week.label: 2–8 January 2025
week.why: Chosen on 2026-11-03 as the 2025 winter week (December to February) with the largest shortfall for this fleet: two windy days, then three calm, cold days.

techs.name: Lithium-ion battery
techs.limit: State of charge between empty and full; most warranties allow about one [[full-cycle|full cycle]] a day.

source.label: DOE, 2022 Grid Energy Storage Technology Cost and Performance Assessment, Table 4.4 (LFP, AC round trip 82.59%, 2021)

techs.name: Pumped storage hydro
techs.limit: Reservoir levels: the usable energy is the water between the upper reservoir's lowest and highest level.

source.label: DOE, 2022 Grid Energy Storage Technology Cost and Performance Assessment, Figure 4.16 (PSH, round trip 80%)

techs.name: Heat store (power to heat to power)
techs.limit: [[standing-loss|Standing loss]]: a hot store cools a little every hour, full or not; 2% a day here (an illustrative assumption).

source.label: DOE, 2022 assessment, p. 85 (a particle thermal store's expected round trip, 50%)

lossSource.label: Illustrative, borrowed from a design target: NREL/CP-5700-77910 (2020), a molten-salt tank's insulation designed for at most 2% heat loss in 24 hours

techs.name: Hydrogen in a salt cavern
techs.limit: Conversion losses: [[electrolyzer|electrolyzer]] in, [[fuel-cell|fuel cell]] out; 31% of what goes in comes back.

source.label: DOE, 2022 Grid Energy Storage Technology Cost and Performance Assessment, Figure 4.27 (hydrogen: electrolyzer, cavern, fuel cell; round trip 31%)
DOE Office of Technology Transitions, Pathways to Commercial Liftoff: Long Duration Energy Storage Opportunities (summit slides 13 and 14, 27 July 2023)

cards.why: DOE's chart puts flywheels at minutes: a spinning mass gives power fast but holds little energy.
U.S. batteries built through 2020 averaged about 3 hours at full power (EIA, 2022).
DOE gives 0 to 15 hours for traditional pumped storage; an 8-hour plant sits in the short-duration bin.

cards.text: Liquid air (air chilled to a liquid, later warmed to drive a turbine)

cards.why: Iron rusts as it discharges and is restored as it charges. DOE gives metal-anode batteries, iron-air among them, 50 to 200 hours: multi-day.

cards.text: Hydrogen in a salt cavern, weeks of output
cards.why: Weeks are more than 160 hours; DOE's seasonal bin is mainly chemical storage, a fuel that keeps.

ladder.note: Cards with a range that spans two bins carry one example rating (an 8-hour pumped storage plant, a 100-hour iron-air battery), so each has one right bin.

costs.about: Total installed costs of 100 MW systems in the report's own sizes, from data gathered in 2021 (the report's 'current' year; it states no other dollar year). One source, one year. Fixed operation and maintenance, cycling wear and replacements are left out.

items.name: Lithium-ion battery
items.page: p. vii; Figure 4.3, calendar life 16 years

source.label: DOE, Energy Storage Grand Challenge, 2022 Grid Energy Storage Technology Cost and Performance Assessment (PNNL-33283, August 2022)

costs.cycleRule: A full cycle takes the duration to discharge plus the duration ÷ round trip to recharge at full power (the report's own example: a 2-hour store at 80% runs 4.5 hours a cycle); at most one cycle a day, as most battery warranties allow (the same report).

facts.what: Average monthly round-trip efficiency of U.S. utility-scale batteries and of pumped storage plants in 2019.
U.S. pumped storage hydro capacity in 2025, in 18 states.
facts.source: EIA, Energy Explained: where hydropower is generated

facts.what: DOE's Long Duration Storage Shot (2021): 90% lower cost by 2030, against a 2020 lithium-ion baseline, for storage of 10 or more hours.
facts.source: DOE Office of Electricity, Achieving the Promise of Low-Cost Long Duration Energy Storage, p. iii

facts.what: Full cycles of 24- and 100-hour stores: their yearly output, and so their cost per MWh, is limited by how often they can cycle.
facts.source: DOE, 2022 Grid Energy Storage Technology Cost and Performance Assessment, p. viii

reference.about: Results of the lesson's week, solved with HiGHS 1.15.1 once for each store (unserved energy and the share of the shortfall covered), and the week's shortfall figures the page states. Energy in MWh.
